articles.title: UC Davis spinout Delix Therapeutics raises USD 100m Series C after Phase Ib MDD data
articles.snippet: UC Davis spinout Delix Therapeutics raises USD 100m Series C after Phase Ib MDD data AllSci
articles.text:
Massachusetts-based Delix Therapeutics closed a USD 100 million Series C financing to take zalsupindole into Phase II. The company said a Phase Ib trial in adults with recurrent major depressive disorder (MDD) produced an approximately 50% mean reduction in Montgomery-Åsberg Depression Rating Scale scores at Day 8, maintained through Day 36. ​
Johnson & Johnson, through Johnson & Johnson Innovation – JJDC, Inc., and SV Health Investors' Dementia Discovery Fund led the round. Existing investors RA Capital, UC Investments, Artis Ventures, OMX Ventures, Dolby Family Ventures, and Bail Capital participated, as did new investors including Adage Capital Management, Hamilton Square Partners Management, Vestal Point Capital, and YK Bioventures. Christian Jung of SV Health Investors and a JJDC representative have joined the board. The company's previous financings include a USD 70 million Series A in September 2021 and a convertible note financing of more than USD 30 million in January 2022 .
Zalsupindole is an orally bioavailable neuroplastogen inspired by 5-MeO-DMT (mebufotenin). Delix says it is engineered to promote structural and functional neuroplasticity without hallucinatory, dissociative, sedative, or other psychotomimetic effects. The company reported no such effects across more than 120 participants studied to date. It expects to start a placebo-controlled Phase II proof-of-concept trial in recurrent MDD in the first half of 2027, with a trial design that includes at-home administration.
Proceeds will also fund additional development candidates and expansion of the company's neurodegeneration program, which the company says has shown preclinical efficacy signals. The platform traces to the lab of David E. Olson at the University of California, Davis , which identifies Delix as a spinout. David E. Olson co-founded the company.

articles.text:
XLIO Secures Additional $100 Million to Build Startups for Corporate Acquirers
News provided by
XLIO Ventures
10 Nov, 2026, 13:30 GMT
Share this article
Share this article
Global Made to Order™ startup builder to add Austin office, led by CEO Ron Kornfeld
AUSTIN, Texas , Nov. 10, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- XLIO has secured an additional $100 million to make its total available funding facility $150 Million. The funds will be deployed to build Made to Order startups for leading technology companies. CEO Ron Kornfeld will lead its new Austin, Texas office.
Made to Order gives organizations a different route to access new technology. Rather than buying an existing company and adapting it, a client defines the exact capability it needs. XLIO then funds and builds a dedicated startup to deliver it, located and incorporated wherever best suits the client. Once the company hits agreed KPIs, usually within one to three years, the client acquires both team and technology. Deals typically range from $10 million to $50 million.
The new funding allows XLIO to run more Made to Order engagements in parallel and to extend the model into both new sectors and geographies.
The Austin office, at 801 Barton Springs Rd, Austin 78704, Texas, puts XLIO close to the engineering talent, founders and corporate buyers that Made to Order is designed for. Austin-based startups raised a record $7.19 billion in venture funding in 2025, up 64.8% on 2024, according to Crunchbase.
That startup economy in the region has deep roots. IBM, Texas Instruments and Motorola opened operations in Austin between 1967 and 1974, and Dell was founded in the city in 1984. Their early presence built the engineering talent base that later drew the headquarters of companies such as Tesla to the region and now feeds a new generation of startups.
"Austin's startup economy is vibrant," said Ron Kornfeld, CEO of XLIO Ventures. "There's deep engineering talent here, a steady stream of experienced founders, and a business community that backs new companies. I've moved here because I want our clients to share in that. Made to Order lets a business tap into Austin's talent and pace to get the exact technology it needs, built by a team focused on nothing else. This funding means we can help many more of them gain a foothold here."
About XLIO
Founded in 2020 and headquartered in London and Seattle, XLIO Ventures gives organizations a new route to acquire the technology they need. Through its Made to Order™ model, XLIO funds and builds a dedicated technology company around a single client's exact need, then transfers it to the client through acquisition only once agreed performance goals are met. Led by CEO Ron Kornfeld and backed by private equity, XLIO works with technology vendors and other large organizations that build advantage by investing in their own proprietary technology. Learn more at xl.io.

South African fintech Yoco secures $100 million credit facility from Victory Park Capital Advisors
0
By
Tapiwa Matthew Mutisi
on
November 9, 2026
Africa , Fintech , Funding , Investments , SMEs , Startups
Yoco Technologies , the South African fintech company backed by global private equity firm TPG Inc., has secured a $100 million credit facility from Victory Park Capital Advisors LLC (VPC), a U.S.-based alternative investment manager with approximately $3.6 billion in assets under management.
The funding represents a significant milestone for Yoco as it continues expanding its financial services ecosystem for small and medium-sized businesses (SMEs) across South Africa.
Funding to Expand Merchant Financing
According to reports, Yoco plans to use the new credit facility to strengthen and expand financing opportunities available to its growing network of merchants.
The company has evolved beyond its origins as a point-of-sale (POS) payments provider and now offers a broader suite of digital commerce solutions designed to help small businesses accept payments, manage operations, and access working capital.
The $100 million facility will enable Yoco to extend additional funding to merchants that use its platform, helping business owners access capital needed to purchase inventory, invest in growth, manage cash flow, or navigate seasonal fluctuations.
Access to affordable financing remains one of the biggest challenges facing SMEs in South Africa, making merchant-lending solutions an increasingly important area of growth for fintech companies.
Yoco’s Evolution Into a Full-Service Fintech Platform
Founded in 2015, Yoco initially built its reputation by providing simple card payment devices and digital payment solutions to small businesses that were often underserved by traditional banks.
Over time, the company expanded its offering to include:
Payment acceptance solutions
Point-of-sale systems
Business management tools
Online payment services
Merchant cash advances and financing products
Digital commerce solutions
Today, Yoco serves hundreds of thousands of merchants across South Africa, ranging from informal traders and restaurants to retail stores and service-based businesses.
The company’s technology-driven approach enables it to analyse transaction histories and business performance data, allowing it to offer financing products tailored to merchants’ actual business activity rather than relying solely on traditional credit assessments.
Strategic Backing From TPG
Yoco has attracted significant investor interest in recent years, including backing from TPG Inc. , one of the world’s largest private equity and alternative asset management firms. The involvement of TPG has provided Yoco with additional capital and strategic support as it expands its footprint within South Africa’s rapidly growing digital payments market.
The latest facility from Victory Park Capital further strengthens Yoco’s ability to scale its lending operations without diluting existing shareholders, as debt financing allows the company to access growth capital while maintaining ownership structures.
Victory Park Capital’s Growing Fintech Portfolio
Victory Park Capital has become an active investor in financial technology and alternative lending businesses globally.
The firm specializes in providing flexible capital solutions to companies operating in sectors such as:
Financial services
Fintech
Consumer lending
Asset-backed finance
Small business financing

articles.title: As AI Threats Surge, Daylight Raises $80M Led by Goldman Sachs Alternatives
articles.snippet: As AI Threats Surge, Daylight Raises $80M Led by Goldman Sachs Alternatives The Globe and Mail
articles.text:
NEW YORK CITY, NY / ACCESS Newswire / November 10, 2026 / Daylight, which combines AI agents with human security experts to detect, investigate, and respond to cyber threats, today announced an $80 million Series B led by Growth Equity at Goldman Sachs Alternatives, with existing investors Bain Capital, Craft Ventures, Vintage Partners, and Maple Capital. The round brings Daylight's total funding to $120 million. Daylight's revenue has surged more than 40x over the past year, fueled by rapidly growing demand from Fortune 500 enterprises and leading AI-native companies. Its customer base includes Lovable, LastPass, Rogo, dLocal, and Miro.
October's wave of cyber incidents, dubbed "Black October," stretched incident response teams already under pressure from increasingly complex security threats. As organizations turn to AI to help manage these mounting demands, the technology isn't necessarily easing the burden. A July 2026 ISC2 survey found that 65% of cybersecurity professionals using AI now spend more time determining whether to trust its recommendations than they did a year ago, while 63% spend more time verifying its outputs.
The challenge goes beyond AI adoption. Companies also struggle to find security services that fit their specific needs. Traditional managed security providers offer rigid, one-size-fits-all services, while standalone AI tools often leave companies managing yet another system. Some organizations want to outsource security operations entirely, while others have internal teams and want to retain control over their detections and processes. As a result, enterprises are left piecing together multiple vendors for detection and response, threat hunting, phishing, data protection, and security data management.
Daylight brings these capabilities together through a flexible service model that combines AI automation with some of the world's top security engineering talent, expertise that most companies struggle to recruit and retain. Its AI-native platform and security engineers continuously build, run, and customize AI agents to each customer's systems, workflows, risks, and priorities. The agents handle day-to-day security operations, while engineers focus on decisions requiring human judgment. Customers can choose how the service is delivered, whether fully managed, co-managed alongside their internal teams, or supported by forward-deployed engineers.
Daylight detects threats in seconds and responds to and contains them within minutes, up to 10 times faster than traditional managed security providers. Customers can run leaner security teams without sacrificing the expertise needed to protect their businesses, as AI agents take on routine operations and experienced security engineers handle complex decisions. Through Aura, Daylight's AI-native platform, customers can also investigate their security environment using natural language, access their security data in a centralized data lake, and manage their security operations from one place.
Daylight's coverage also extends to the AI platforms enterprises use themselves, protecting against AI-native risks like prompt injection, risky MCPs, and unusual AI-driven activity. Those detections run through Daylight's full MDR workflow, where AI activity is investigated alongside identity, endpoint, cloud, SaaS, and business context. The capability is already in use by enterprise customers, including Miro.

The investment will support the development of specialized chips designed to improve the efficiency of AI inference by concentrating computing resources on the operations that are needed. The round was led by ICM HPQC Fund, with participation from Lockheed Martin Ventures, GlobalFoundries, GS Futures, Cloudberry Ventures, TGFS, and the European Innovation Council Fund.
